issues.title: Reversed inequality in SGD lower bound invalidates relative performance guarantee
issues.why_classification: Theorem 2 is a central theoretical result of the paper, promising that MKL-SGD stationary points provably outperform the SGD fixed point. Because SGD can converge arbitrarily close to $\ws$ when outlier gradients cancel, no comparable relative bound holds without new assumptions and a new proof architecture.

issues.failure_explanation: Lemma 4 asserts that the bound $\norm{\wsm - \ws} \leq \frac{\epsilon^k G}{\lambda}$ holds for 'any first order stationary point attained by MKL-SGD'. In its proof, the author bounds the sum of outlier selection probabilities by $\sum_{i\in\mathcal{O}} p_i(\wsm) \leq \epsilon^k$. However, this probability bound is only valid when $\wsm$ lies in the basin $\mathcal{B}_r(\ws)$ where all clean samples have lower loss than all outliers. Outside $\mathcal{B}_r(\ws)$, such as near an outlier cluster $w_B$, outliers have smaller loss than clean samples, so the probability of selecting an outlier is $1 - (1-\epsilon)^k$, which approaches 1 rather than $\epsilon^k$. As the paper itself emphasizes in Section 4.2, spurious local minima can exist near $w_B$ at distance at least $2\delta$ from $\ws$, so the claim does not hold for arbitrary stationary points.
issues.least_adequate_overall_repair: Restrict the statement of Lemma 4 to stationary points $\wsm \in \mathcal{B}_r(\ws)$, matching the restriction already stated in Theorem 2.
issues.overall_effect: The claim that every stationary point of MKL-SGD is within $\frac{\epsilon^k G}{\lambda}$ of $\ws$ fails; the guarantee is unreliable for stationary points outside $\mathcal{B}_r(\ws)$.
issues.title: Universal quantification over all stationary points in MKL distance bound
issues.why_classification: Adding the hypothesis $\wsm \in \mathcal{B}_r(\ws)$ resolves the mismatch and aligns Lemma 4 with its proof and Theorem 2, but requires retracting the substantive claim that all local minima of MKL-SGD satisfy the bound.
